title: Styling Images with CSS knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Styling Images with CSS”?
questions.explanation: The source curriculum lists “The width and height properties” under “Styling Images with CSS”. The lesson applies this syllabus point to a small CSS example and a browser check.

questions.prompt: Which practice best supports reliable work with styling images with css?
options: Preserve aspect ratio, avoid layout shifts, and provide appropriate alternatives for meaningful content.
Add !important to every declaration so conflicts disappear.
Assume the newest CSS feature behaves identically in all browsers.
Remove focus styles because a mouse user can see the hovered element.
questions.answer_key: Preserve aspect ratio, avoid layout shifts, and provide appropriate alternatives for meaningful content.
questions.explanation: The key practice is: Preserve aspect ratio, avoid layout shifts, and provide appropriate alternatives for meaningful content. For advanced features, inspect the relevant documentation and target-browser compatibility.

questions.prompt: If an example related to “Styling Images with CSS” does not look or behave as expected, what is the strongest first response?
options: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
Add several unrelated overrides until the screenshot looks closer.
Only check the default viewport and skip interactive states.
Treat an unused declaration as proof that the browser is broken.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
questions.explanation: A repeatable inspection loop is more reliable than layering on overrides: inspect what matched, identify the computed value, change one cause, and retest.
